source.text: Λέγετέ μοι, οἱ ὑπὸ νόμον θέλοντες εἶναι, τὸν νόμον οὐκ ἀκούετε;

records.literal_gloss: Tell me, those under law wishing to be, the law not do you hear?

en.L: Tell me, you who want to be under [the] law, do you not listen to the law?
en.B: You who want to be under the law, tell me: do you not hear what the law says?
en.R: You want to live under the law. Then tell me, do you not listen to what the law itself says?

es.L: {{plural_you:Díganme|Decidme}}, {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} que {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} estar bajo [la] ley, ¿no {{plural_you:escuchan|escucháis}} la ley?
es.B: {{plural_you:Ustedes|Vosotros}}, los que {{plural_you:quieren|queréis}} estar bajo la ley, {{plural_you:díganme|decidme}}: ¿no {{plural_you:escuchan|escucháis}} lo que dice la ley?
es.R: {{plural_you:Quieren|Queréis}} vivir bajo la ley. Entonces {{plural_you:díganme|decidme}}: ¿no {{plural_you:escuchan|escucháis}} lo que dice la ley misma?

sw.L: Niambieni, ninyi mnaotaka kuwa chini ya sheria, je, hamsikilizi sheria?
sw.B: Ninyi mnaotaka kuwa chini ya sheria, niambieni: je, hamsikii kile ambacho sheria inasema?
sw.R: Mnataka kuishi chini ya sheria. Basi niambieni, je, hamsikilizi kile ambacho sheria yenyewe inasema?

fr.L: Dites-moi, vous qui voulez être sous la Loi, n’écoutez-vous pas la Loi ?
fr.B: Vous qui voulez être sous la Loi, dites-moi : n’entendez-vous pas ce que dit la Loi ?
fr.R: Vous voulez vivre sous la Loi. Alors dites-moi : est-ce que vous n’écoutez pas ce que la Loi elle-même dit ?

decisions.choice: the law the second time: the books of Moses as Scripture, here the story in Genesis
alternatives: the same sense both times: the commandments
decisions.reason: Paul uses νόμον twice with two senses. "Under law" is the law of Moses as a way of life that rules a person (3:23, 4:4-5). "The law" they should listen to is the written Law, the five books of Moses, which include the story of Abraham's sons that he is about to tell (Genesis 16-21). His point is that the law itself speaks against what they want.

decisions.choice: listen to: hear with understanding and take to heart
decisions.reason: ἀκούω can mean simply to hear a text read aloud, as the law was read in the synagogues, but here Paul asks whether they really hear what it says. The question expects the answer that they do not.

decisions.choice: those who want to be under law: people still deciding, drawn toward it
decisions.reason: The present participle θέλοντες describes what the Galatians wish for now. They have not yet taken on the law in full; Paul is warning them before they do (compare 4:9-10, 5:2-3).

decisions.choice: You want to live under the law. Then tell me ... what the law itself says
alternatives: Tell me, you who want to be under the law, do you not listen to the law?
decisions.reason: Readable splits the question in two and adds "itself" to show the turn in Paul's argument: the law they want points away from the law (m1).

decisions.choice: ustedes / vosotros forms
decisions.reason: Paul addresses the Galatians in the plural. As elsewhere in his letters, each plural "you" and its verb is a reader setting: ustedes (Latin America, the default) or vosotros (Spain).

decisions.choice: escuchar
decisions.reason: "Oír" can mean only that sound reaches the ear; "escuchar" is to listen and attend, which is the sense of the meaning decision (m2), so every level uses it.

decisions.choice: kusikiliza (L, R); kusikia (B)
decisions.reason: "Kusikia" is to hear, "kusikiliza" to listen with attention. Literal and Readable use "hamsikilizi" for the sense of the meaning decision (m2); Balanced says "hamsikii kile ambacho sheria inasema", where hearing what the law says carries the same point.

decisions.choice: la Loi, with a capital, both times
decisions.reason: Paul uses the word first for the law of Moses as a rule of life and then for the books of Moses as Scripture (m1). Both are the Law given through Moses, so French writes both with the capital; Readable's "elle-même" shows the turn in the argument, as the English "itself" does.

source.text: γέγραπται γὰρ ὅτι Ἀβραὰμ δύο υἱοὺς ἔσχεν, ἕνα ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης καὶ ἕνα ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας·

records.literal_gloss: It has been written for that Abraham two sons had, one from the slave woman and one from the free.

en.L: For it is written that Abraham had two sons, one from the slave woman and one from the free [woman].
en.B: Scripture says that Abraham had two sons: one was the son of the slave woman, the other the son of the free woman.
en.R: The Scriptures say that Abraham had two sons. One son's mother was a slave woman. The other son's mother was a free woman.

es.L: Porque está escrito que Abraham tuvo dos hijos, uno de la esclava y uno de la libre.
es.B: La Escritura dice que Abraham tuvo dos hijos: uno fue hijo de la esclava, y el otro, hijo de la mujer libre.
es.R: Las Escrituras dicen que Abraham tuvo dos hijos. La madre de uno era una esclava. La madre del otro era una mujer libre.

sw.L: Kwa maana imeandikwa kwamba Ibrahimu alikuwa na wana wawili, mmoja kutoka kwa mwanamke mtumwa na mmoja kutoka kwa [mwanamke] huru.
sw.B: Maandiko yanasema kwamba Ibrahimu alikuwa na wana wawili: mmoja alikuwa mwana wa mwanamke mtumwa, na mwingine mwana wa mwanamke huru.
sw.R: Maandiko yanasema kwamba Ibrahimu alikuwa na wana wawili. Mama wa mwana mmoja alikuwa mtumwa. Mama wa yule mwingine alikuwa mwanamke huru.

fr.L: Car il est écrit qu’Abraham a eu deux fils, un de l’esclave et un de la [femme] libre.
fr.B: L’Écriture dit qu’Abraham a eu deux fils : l’un était le fils de l’esclave, l’autre le fils de la femme libre.
fr.R: Les Écritures disent qu’Abraham a eu deux fils. La mère de l’un était une esclave. La mère de l’autre était une femme libre.

decisions.choice: a summary of Genesis 16-21: Ishmael born to Hagar, Isaac born to Sarah
decisions.reason: "It is written" (γέγραπται) introduces not a quotation but a summary of the Genesis story: Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian slave, bore Ishmael to Abraham (Genesis 16:1-4, 15), and Sarah bore Isaac (Genesis 21:1-3). Abraham had other sons later (Genesis 25:1-2); Paul speaks only of these two.

decisions.choice: slave woman: a female slave, owned by her mistress
decisions.reason: παιδίσκη can mean a young girl, but in Paul's day it most often meant a female slave. Genesis 16:1 says Hagar was Sarah's slave, and Paul builds his whole contrast on slave and free (4:23-31, 5:1).

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave woman" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free: the contrast with "free" carries the passage, and "servant" would hide that Hagar was owned. Older words such as "bondwoman" or "handmaid" are no longer plain English.

decisions.choice: free [woman] (L); free woman (B, R)
decisions.reason: ἐλευθέρας is a feminine adjective used as a noun, "the free one", meaning Sarah. English needs "woman".

decisions.choice: Scripture says
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the sense of the set formula "it has been written": this is what Scripture records.

decisions.choice: la esclava ... la libre (L); la mujer libre (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Esclava" is the feminine of "esclavo", the word used for doulos throughout Paul, and keeps the slave/free contrast of the passage; "sierva" and "criada" soften it. Spanish can make the adjective a noun with the article, "la libre", so Literal needs no bracket; Balanced and Readable say "la mujer libre" for clarity.

decisions.choice: mwanamke mtumwa ... mwanamke huru
decisions.reason: "Mjakazi" is the traditional word for a slave woman, but it is now old and can be heard as a maidservant. "Mwanamke mtumwa" uses "mtumwa", the word for doulos throughout Paul, and so keeps the link with "utumwa" (slavery) in verses 24-25 and 5:1; "mwanamke huru" stands against it.

decisions.choice: l'esclave, une esclave at every level (4:22-31)
decisions.reason: Hagar was owned by her mistress (m2), and the whole passage sets slave against free (5:1), so French keeps "esclave" at every level, as the English does. "Servante", the word of older French Bibles, would hide this.

decisions.choice: a eu (passé composé) after "il est écrit que"
decisions.reason: Paul summarizes the Genesis story inside his argument rather than telling it, so French uses the passé composé of discourse at every level; the imparfait "persécutait" in 4:29 keeps the Greek imperfect.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὁ μὲν ἐκ τῆς παιδίσκης κατὰ σάρκα γεγέννηται, ὁ δὲ ἐκ τῆς ἐλευθέρας δι’ ἐπαγγελίας.

records.literal_gloss: But the [one] indeed from the slave woman according to flesh has been born, the [one] but from the free through promise.

en.L: But the [one] from the slave woman was born according to [the] flesh, and the [one] from the free [woman] through [the] promise.
en.B: The slave woman's son was born according to the flesh, but the free woman's son was born through the promise.
en.R: The slave woman's son was born in the ordinary way, through a plan people made. But the free woman's son was born because of what God had promised.

es.L: Pero el de la esclava nació según [la] carne, y el de la libre, por medio de [la] promesa.
es.B: El hijo de la esclava nació según la carne, pero el hijo de la mujer libre nació por la promesa.
es.R: El hijo de la esclava nació de la manera común, por un plan que hicieron las personas. Pero el hijo de la mujer libre nació porque Dios lo había prometido.

sw.L: Lakini yule wa mwanamke mtumwa amezaliwa kulingana na mwili, na yule wa [mwanamke] huru kupitia ahadi.
sw.B: Mwana wa mwanamke mtumwa alizaliwa kufuatana na mwili, lakini mwana wa mwanamke huru alizaliwa kupitia ahadi.
sw.R: Mwana wa mwanamke mtumwa alizaliwa kwa njia ya kawaida, kwa mpango ambao wanadamu walifanya. Lakini mwana wa mwanamke huru alizaliwa kwa sababu ya kile ambacho Mungu alikuwa ameahidi.

fr.L: Mais celui de l’esclave est né selon la chair, et celui de la [femme] libre par la promesse.
fr.B: Le fils de l’esclave est né selon la chair, mais le fils de la femme libre est né grâce à la promesse.
fr.R: Le fils de l’esclave est né de façon ordinaire, à la suite d’un plan imaginé par des gens. Mais le fils de la femme libre est né parce que Dieu l’avait promis.

decisions.choice: according to the flesh: by ordinary human means, as people arranged it
decisions.reason: Here σάρξ is not the sinful self of 5:13-24 but natural human birth. Ishmael was born in the normal course of things, by Sarah's own plan to have a child through Hagar (Genesis 16:2). Isaac was born when Sarah was past bearing, only because God had promised it (Genesis 17:16-19, 18:10-14, 21:1-2).

decisions.choice: through the promise: God's promise to Abraham of a son by Sarah
decisions.reason: ἐπαγγελία links back to 3:16-18, where the inheritance comes by promise and not by law. Isaac's birth is the first proof that God gives what he promises, and does it himself.

decisions.choice: has been born: the birth stands written in Scripture, and its result goes on
decisions.reason: The perfect tense γεγέννηται presents the birth as a fact on record with lasting effect: the two kinds of children still exist (4:28-29).

decisions.choice: the slave woman's son ... the free woman's son
decisions.reason: The Greek has only the article (ὁ), "the one"; the sons of verse 22 are meant.

decisions.choice: in the ordinary way, through a plan people made ... because of what God had promised
alternatives: according to the flesh ... through the promise
decisions.reason: Readable explains the two phrases from the Genesis story (m1, m2). "Flesh" alone would make a young reader think of the body or of sin.

decisions.choice: kufuatana na mwili
decisions.reason: In Galatians 5 Balanced renders this word "asili ya dhambi" (sinful nature), but here the meaning decision (m1) says it is ordinary human birth, not the sinful self. So Balanced keeps "mwili", as the English Balanced keeps "flesh", and verse 29 does the same.

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave woman" at every level, as in 4:22: the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free.

source.text: ἅτινά ἐστιν ἀλληγορούμενα· αὗται γάρ εἰσιν δύο διαθῆκαι, μία μὲν ἀπὸ ὄρους Σινᾶ, εἰς δουλείαν γεννῶσα, ἥτις ἐστὶν Ἁγάρ, τὸ δὲ Ἁγὰρ Σινᾶ ὄρος ἐστὶν ἐν τῇ Ἀραβίᾳ, συστοιχεῖ δὲ τῇ νῦν Ἰερουσαλήμ, δουλεύει γὰρ μετὰ τῶν τέκνων αὐτῆς·

records.literal_gloss: Which things are being allegorized; these for are two covenants, one indeed from mount Sinai, unto slavery bearing, which is Hagar. \v 25 The now Hagar Sinai mountain is in the Arabia, corresponds now to the now Jerusalem, is enslaved for with the children of her.

en.L: These things are spoken allegorically, for these [women] are two covenants: one from Mount Sinai, bearing [children] into slavery, which is Hagar. \v 25 Now Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia, and she corresponds to the present Jerusalem, for she is in slavery with her children.
en.B: These things can be read as an allegory. The two women are two covenants. One comes from Mount Sinai and bears children who will be slaves; this is Hagar. \v 25 Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia, and she matches the Jerusalem of the present time, since she is in slavery together with her children.
en.R: This story is also a picture of something else. The two women stand for two covenants. One covenant came from Mount Sinai, and the children born under it are slaves. That covenant is Hagar. \v 25 Hagar stands for Mount Sinai in Arabia. She is like the city of Jerusalem today, because Jerusalem and her people are living as slaves.

es.L: Estas cosas se dicen alegóricamente, porque estas [mujeres] son dos pactos: uno del monte Sinaí, que da a luz [hijos] para esclavitud, el cual es Agar. \v 25 Ahora bien, Agar es el monte Sinaí en Arabia, y corresponde a la Jerusalén actual, porque está en esclavitud con sus hijos.
es.B: Esto puede leerse como una alegoría. Las dos mujeres son dos pactos. Uno procede del monte Sinaí y da a luz hijos que serán esclavos: ese es Agar. \v 25 Agar representa el monte Sinaí en Arabia, y corresponde a la Jerusalén del tiempo presente, ya que ella está en esclavitud junto con sus hijos.
es.R: Esta historia es también una imagen de otra cosa. Las dos mujeres representan dos pactos. Un pacto vino del monte Sinaí, y los hijos que nacen bajo él son esclavos. Ese pacto es Agar. \v 25 Agar representa el monte Sinaí, en Arabia. Ella es como la ciudad de Jerusalén de hoy, porque Jerusalén y su pueblo viven como esclavos.

sw.L: Mambo haya yanasemwa kwa njia ya mfano, kwa maana [wanawake] hawa ni maagano mawili: moja kutoka mlima Sinai, linalozaa [watoto] kwa utumwa, ambalo ni Hajiri. \v 25 Basi Hajiri ni mlima Sinai katika Uarabuni, naye analingana na Yerusalemu ya sasa, kwa maana yuko utumwani pamoja na watoto wake.
sw.B: Mambo haya yanaweza kusomwa kama mfano wa mambo mengine. Wanawake hao wawili ni maagano mawili. Agano moja linatoka mlima Sinai na kuzaa watoto watakaokuwa watumwa; hilo ndilo Hajiri. \v 25 Hajiri anawakilisha mlima Sinai katika Uarabuni, naye analingana na Yerusalemu ya wakati huu, kwa kuwa yuko utumwani pamoja na watoto wake.
sw.R: Habari hii pia ni picha ya jambo jingine. Wanawake hao wawili wanawakilisha maagano mawili. Agano moja lilitoka mlima Sinai, na watoto wanaozaliwa chini yake ni watumwa. Agano hilo ni Hajiri. \v 25 Hajiri anawakilisha mlima Sinai, katika Uarabuni. Yeye ni kama mji wa Yerusalemu wa leo, kwa sababu Yerusalemu na watu wake wanaishi kama watumwa.

fr.L: Ces choses sont dites de manière allégorique, car ces [femmes] sont deux alliances : l’une, du mont Sinaï, enfantant pour l’esclavage, c’est Agar. \v 25 Or Agar, c’est le mont Sinaï en Arabie, et elle correspond à la Jérusalem actuelle, car elle est esclave avec ses enfants.
fr.B: Ces faits peuvent être lus comme une allégorie. Les deux femmes sont deux alliances. L’une vient du mont Sinaï et donne naissance à des enfants destinés à l’esclavage : c’est Agar. \v 25 Agar représente le mont Sinaï en Arabie, et elle correspond à la Jérusalem d’aujourd’hui, puisqu’elle est en esclavage avec ses enfants.
fr.R: Cette histoire est aussi l’image d’autre chose. Les deux femmes représentent deux alliances. Une alliance est venue du mont Sinaï, et les enfants nés sous cette alliance sont esclaves. Cette alliance, c’est Agar. \v 25 Agar représente le mont Sinaï en Arabie. Elle ressemble à la ville de Jérusalem d’aujourd’hui, car Jérusalem et son peuple vivent en esclaves.

decisions.choice: spoken allegorically: the story also says something beyond itself
alternatives: the story is only a parable and did not happen
a pattern in history (typology) rather than an allegory
decisions.reason: ἀλληγορέω means to speak or read a text so that it carries a further meaning. Paul does not deny that the events happened; he has just told them as history (4:22-23). He reads the two mothers and their sons as pictures of two covenants and the people who belong to each.

decisions.choice: these are two covenants: the two women stand for two covenants
decisions.reason: αὗται is feminine and points back to the two women. "Are" means "represent", as Hagar "is" Mount Sinai in verse 25.

decisions.choice: one ...: the second covenant is never named
decisions.reason: μία μὲν ("one on the one hand") leads the reader to expect "the other ...", but Paul never states it. He moves to the Jerusalem above in verse 26, which takes the place of the second covenant and of Sarah, who is not named either. The covenant of promise made with Abraham (3:15-18) is meant.

decisions.choice: bearing children into slavery: those born under the Sinai covenant are slaves under the law
decisions.reason: As Hagar, a slave, bore a son who was a slave, so the covenant given at Sinai produces people who live under the law as slaves. Paul has said this already in 4:1-3 and 4:8-9 and says it again in 5:1.

decisions.choice: Now Hagar is Mount Sinai: the SBLGNT reading, with Hagar's name
alternatives: For Sinai is a mountain in Arabia
decisions.reason: Manuscripts differ here. Some have "for" in place of "now", and some leave out the name Hagar, giving "for Sinai is a mountain in Arabia", a plain remark of geography. The SBLGNT keeps the name. The neuter article before Hagar's name treats it as a word or a figure: "this Hagar" of the allegory. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Arabia: the lands south and east of Judea, outside the land of promise
decisions.reason: In Paul's day "Arabia" covered the desert lands from the Sinai peninsula to beyond the Jordan, where Paul himself went after his conversion (1:17). Hagar's son Ishmael and his descendants lived in this region (Genesis 21:21, 25:12-18). So the mountain where the law was given lies in Hagar's country, outside the land promised to Abraham.

decisions.choice: corresponds to: stands in the same column as the present Jerusalem
decisions.reason: συστοιχέω means to stand in the same row or line, like soldiers in a file. Paul sets out two columns: Hagar, Sinai, slavery and the present Jerusalem in one; Sarah, promise, freedom and the Jerusalem above in the other (4:26). "The present Jerusalem" is the city as the center of life under the law, from which the teachers pressing circumcision drew their authority (compare 2:12).

decisions.choice: in slavery with her children: Jerusalem and its people are slaves under the law
decisions.reason: A city is often pictured as a mother and its people as her children. The slavery is the one Paul has been describing, under the law (4:3, 4:9, 5:1). Jerusalem was also under Roman rule, but that is not Paul's point.

decisions.choice: these [women] (L); The two women (B, R)
decisions.reason: English needs a noun for the feminine pronoun (m2).

decisions.choice: stands for
decisions.reason: The verb "is" here means "represents" (m2). Balanced and Readable say so; Literal keeps "is".

decisions.choice: This story is also a picture of something else ... Jerusalem and her people are living as slaves
alternatives: These things are an allegory ... she is in slavery with her children
decisions.reason: Readable avoids the word "allegory" and says that the story is also a picture (m1). It names "her children" as Jerusalem's people (m8).

decisions.choice: el cual es Agar (L); ese es Agar (B); Ese pacto es Agar (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek relative is feminine because "covenant" is feminine in Greek. Spanish "pacto", the word used for covenant elsewhere in Paul, is masculine, so the pronoun agrees with "pacto" and not with Hagar; Readable names the covenant to make this plain.

decisions.choice: kwa njia ya mfano (L); kama mfano wa mambo mengine (B)
decisions.reason: Swahili has no common word for allegory. "Fumbo" is a riddle or hidden saying and would suggest the story is not history, which the meaning decision (m1) denies; "mfano" (a figure, a picture of something) says that the story stands for something beyond itself.

decisions.choice: slaves / in slavery
decisions.reason: "Slave" at every level, as the style guide keeps it where slavery under the law or the elemental forces is set against freedom (Galatians 4–5). Hagar and Sinai stand in the column of slavery against Sarah and freedom (m4, m7, m8).

decisions.choice: alliances; Agar, Sinaï, Arabie
decisions.reason: "Alliance" as in 3:17: here the word names covenants, not wills. Hagar has her usual French name, "Agar".

source.text: ἡ δὲ ἄνω Ἰερουσαλὴμ ἐλευθέρα ἐστίν, ἥτις ἐστὶν μήτηρ ἡμῶν·

records.literal_gloss: The but above Jerusalem free is, who is mother of us.

en.L: But the Jerusalem above is free, which is our mother.
en.B: The Jerusalem above, however, is free, and it is she who is our mother.
en.R: But there is another Jerusalem, God's city in heaven. She is free, and she is our mother.

es.L: Pero la Jerusalén de arriba es libre, la cual es nuestra madre.
es.B: La Jerusalén de arriba, en cambio, es libre, y ella es nuestra madre.
es.R: Pero hay otra Jerusalén, la ciudad de Dios en el cielo. Ella es libre, y es nuestra madre.

sw.L: Lakini Yerusalemu ya juu ni huru, ambayo ni mama yetu.
sw.B: Lakini Yerusalemu iliyo juu ni huru, nayo ndiyo mama yetu.
sw.R: Lakini kuna Yerusalemu nyingine, mji wa Mungu ulioko mbinguni. Mji huo ni huru, nao ni mama yetu.

fr.L: Mais la Jérusalem d’en haut est libre, elle qui est notre mère.
fr.B: La Jérusalem d’en haut, au contraire, est libre, et c’est elle qui est notre mère.
fr.R: Mais il y a une autre Jérusalem, la ville de Dieu dans le ciel. Elle est libre, et elle est notre mère.

decisions.choice: the Jerusalem above: God's heavenly city, where he reigns and his people belong
decisions.reason: ἄνω ("above") is set against "present" (νῦν) in verse 25. Paul contrasts not two places on earth but the city of this age with the city of God, which belongs to the age to come and is already the home of believers. Compare Philippians 3:20, Hebrews 12:22 and Revelation 21:2.

decisions.choice: who is our mother: the free woman of the allegory, standing where Sarah stands
decisions.reason: Paul does not name Sarah, but the Jerusalem above takes her place as the free woman whose children are free (4:31). "Our" includes Paul, a Jew, and the Galatians, Gentiles: all who believe are her children.

decisions.choice: our mother: the SBLGNT reading
decisions.reason: Many later manuscripts add a word meaning "all", giving "the mother of us all", the reading of the King James Version. The earliest manuscripts do not have it. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: there is another Jerusalem, God's city in heaven
decisions.reason: "The Jerusalem above" would puzzle a young reader; Readable says what it is (m1).

source.text: γέγραπται γάρ· Εὐφράνθητι, στεῖρα ἡ οὐ τίκτουσα, ῥῆξον καὶ βόησον, ἡ οὐκ ὠδίνουσα· ὅτι πολλὰ τὰ τέκνα τῆς ἐρήμου μᾶλλον ἢ τῆς ἐχούσης τὸν ἄνδρα.

records.literal_gloss: It has been written for: Rejoice, barren [one] the not bearing, break forth and shout, the not travailing; because many the children of the desolate more than of the [one] having the husband.

en.L: For it is written: "Rejoice, barren [woman] who does not bear; break out and shout, you who are not in labor; for many [are] the children of the desolate [woman], more than of her who has the husband."
en.B: For it is written: "Be glad, barren woman, you who have borne no child; break into a shout, you who have never been in labor. For the woman left alone has many children, more than the woman who has a husband."
en.R: The Scriptures say, "Be glad, you woman who could never have children! You never felt the pains of giving birth, but now break out and shout for joy! The woman who was left alone has more children than the woman who has a husband."

es.L: Porque está escrito: «Regocíjate, estéril que no das a luz; irrumpe y grita, tú que no estás de parto; porque muchos [son] los hijos de la desolada, más que de la que tiene el marido».
es.B: Porque está escrito: «Alégrate, mujer estéril, tú que no has dado a luz; estalla en gritos, tú que nunca has tenido dolores de parto. Porque la mujer abandonada tiene muchos hijos, más que la que tiene marido».
es.R: Las Escrituras dicen: «¡Alégrate, mujer que nunca pudiste tener hijos! Nunca sentiste los dolores del parto, pero ahora ¡rompe a gritar de alegría! La mujer que fue dejada sola tiene más hijos que la mujer que tiene marido».

sw.L: Kwa maana imeandikwa: "Furahi, [mwanamke] tasa usiyezaa; lipuka na upige kelele, wewe usiyepatwa na uchungu wa kuzaa; kwa maana watoto wa [mwanamke] aliyeachwa ukiwa ni wengi, kuliko wa yule aliye na mume."
sw.B: Kwa maana imeandikwa: "Shangilia, mwanamke tasa, wewe ambaye hujapata kuzaa; lipuka kwa kelele, wewe ambaye hujawahi kupatwa na uchungu wa kuzaa. Kwa maana mwanamke aliyeachwa peke yake ana watoto wengi, kuliko yule aliye na mume."
sw.R: Maandiko yanasema, "Furahi, wewe mwanamke ambaye hukuweza kamwe kupata watoto! Hukuwahi kuona uchungu wa kuzaa, lakini sasa lipuka, upige kelele za furaha! Mwanamke aliyeachwa peke yake ana watoto wengi kuliko yule aliye na mume."

fr.L: Car il est écrit : « Réjouis-toi, stérile, toi qui n’enfantes pas ; éclate et crie, toi qui n’es pas en travail ; car nombreux [sont] les enfants de la délaissée, plus que [ceux] de celle qui a le mari. »
fr.B: Car il est écrit : « Sois dans la joie, femme stérile, toi qui n’as pas eu d’enfant ; éclate en cris, toi qui n’as pas connu les douleurs de l’enfantement. Car la femme délaissée a beaucoup d’enfants, plus que la femme qui a un mari. »
fr.R: Les Écritures disent : « Réjouis-toi, toi la femme qui n’as jamais pu avoir d’enfants ! Tu n’as jamais connu les douleurs de l’accouchement, mais maintenant, éclate en cris de joie ! La femme qui a été laissée seule a plus d’enfants que la femme qui a un mari. »

decisions.choice: a quotation of Isaiah 54:1, word for word as in the Greek Old Testament
decisions.reason: Isaiah speaks to Jerusalem after the exile as a barren woman, abandoned and childless, and promises that her children will be more than she can count. Paul joins the barren woman to Sarah, who was barren (Genesis 11:30) and became the mother of the promised son, and so to the Jerusalem above (4:26). The many children are those who now believe, Gentiles among them.

decisions.choice: the desolate woman: a woman left alone, deserted
decisions.reason: ἔρημος can mean a desert, but here it describes a woman without husband or children, as Jerusalem was left desolate in exile (Isaiah 54:4-6).

decisions.choice: the woman who has the husband: in Paul's reading, Hagar
alternatives: only Isaiah's picture, with no application to Hagar
decisions.reason: In Isaiah the married woman stands for a city with all its people. Paul seems to apply her to Hagar, whom Sarah gave to Abraham as a wife (Genesis 16:3) and who bore him a son, while Sarah stayed barren. He does not say this outright, so the link is likely rather than certain.

decisions.choice: break forth and shout: burst out in a cry of joy
decisions.reason: ῥήγνυμι means to break or burst; with "shout" it pictures someone bursting into a joyful cry, as in Isaiah 49:13, where the hills break into song.

decisions.choice: the woman left alone has many children, more than (B); has more children than (R)
alternatives: more are the children of the desolate
decisions.reason: The Greek has no verb; Balanced and Readable supply "has" to make a sentence. "Left alone" is plainer than "desolate" (m2).

decisions.choice: but now break out and shout for joy
decisions.reason: Readable adds "for joy" (m4) and "now" to mark the change from her past grief.

decisions.choice: tú forms, no setting
decisions.reason: The prophet speaks to one woman, so the imperatives are singular "tú" forms ("Alégrate", "estalla") and are not under the plural_you setting.

decisions.choice: lipuka
decisions.reason: The verb means to break or burst (m4). "Lipuka" (burst out) keeps that picture of a sudden cry; "paza sauti" (raise the voice) is weaker.

decisions.choice: la délaissée (L); la femme délaissée (B); laissée seule (R)
decisions.reason: The word describes a woman left without husband or children (m2); "délaissée" says this in current French, while "désolée" now means only "sorry".

source.text: ὑμεῖς δέ, ἀδελφοί, κατὰ Ἰσαὰκ ἐπαγγελίας τέκνα ἐστέ·

records.literal_gloss: You now, brothers, like Isaac of promise children are.

en.L: But you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, are children of promise like Isaac.
en.B: And you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, are children of the promise, as Isaac was.
en.R: And you, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, are like Isaac. You are children born because of what God promised.

es.L: Pero {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos, {{plural_you:son|sois}} hijos de [la] promesa como Isaac.
es.B: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos, {{plural_you:son|sois}} hijos de la promesa, como lo fue Isaac.
es.R: Y {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, hermanos, {{plural_you:son|sois}} como Isaac. {{plural_you:Son|Sois}} hijos que nacieron por lo que Dios había prometido.

sw.L: Lakini ninyi, ndugu, ni watoto wa ahadi kama Isaka.
sw.B: Nanyi, ndugu, ni watoto wa ahadi, kama Isaka alivyokuwa.
sw.R: Nanyi, ndugu, mko kama Isaka. Ninyi ni watoto mliozaliwa kwa sababu ya kile ambacho Mungu aliahidi.

fr.L: Mais vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, vous êtes enfants de la promesse, à la manière d’Isaac.
fr.B: Et vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, vous êtes enfants de la promesse, comme Isaac.
fr.R: Et vous, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, vous êtes comme Isaac. Vous êtes des enfants nés parce que Dieu l’a promis.

decisions.choice: like Isaac: after the pattern of Isaac
decisions.reason: κατὰ with a name means "in the manner of". The Galatians were not born of Sarah, but like Isaac they owe their place in Abraham's family to God's promise, not to human descent or effort (3:29).

decisions.choice: children of promise: children whose life in God's family comes from his promise
decisions.reason: Isaac was born because God promised him (4:23). In the same way the Galatians, Gentiles who believed, became Abraham's children through the promise given to Abraham and fulfilled in Christ (3:14, 3:29).

decisions.choice: you are: the SBLGNT reading
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "we are" here, matching "our mother" in verse 26 and "we are" in verse 31. The SBLGNT reads "you are", and the change to "we" is easier to explain as a scribe's smoothing than the reverse. Reviewers must check the apparatus.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul is writing to the whole church in Galatia, women and men, and has just said that in Christ there is neither male nor female (3:28). "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: children born because of what God promised
decisions.reason: Readable explains "children of promise" from verse 23 (m2).

decisions.choice: hermanos, no setting
decisions.reason: As elsewhere in Paul, Spanish "hermanos" already covers brothers and sisters, so there is no gender span here or in verse 31.

decisions.choice: ndugu, no setting
alternatives: ndugu wa kiume na wa kike
decisions.reason: "Ndugu" already means brothers and sisters, so Swahili has no gender span here or in verse 31.

source.text: ἀλλ’ ὥσπερ τότε ὁ κατὰ σάρκα γεννηθεὶς ἐδίωκε τὸν κατὰ πνεῦμα, οὕτως καὶ νῦν.

records.literal_gloss: But just as then the [one] according to flesh having been born was persecuting the [one] according to Spirit, so also now.

en.L: But just as at that time the [one] born according to [the] flesh persecuted the [one born] according to [the] Spirit, so [it is] also now.
en.B: In those days the son born according to the flesh persecuted the son born according to the Spirit, and it is the same now.
en.R: But back then, the son born in the ordinary human way mistreated the son born by the power of the Spirit. The same thing is happening now.

es.L: Pero así como entonces el que nació según [la] carne perseguía al [nacido] según [el] Espíritu, así también ahora.
es.B: En aquel tiempo el hijo nacido según la carne perseguía al hijo nacido según el Espíritu, y lo mismo sucede ahora.
es.R: Pero en aquel tiempo, el hijo que nació de la manera humana común maltrataba al hijo que nació por el poder del Espíritu. Lo mismo está pasando ahora.

sw.L: Lakini kama vile wakati ule yule aliyezaliwa kulingana na mwili alikuwa akimtesa yule [aliyezaliwa] kulingana na Roho, ndivyo [ilivyo] sasa pia.
sw.B: Wakati ule mwana aliyezaliwa kufuatana na mwili alimtesa mwana aliyezaliwa kufuatana na Roho, na ndivyo ilivyo sasa.
sw.R: Lakini zamani zile, mwana aliyezaliwa kwa njia ya kawaida ya kibinadamu alimtendea vibaya mwana aliyezaliwa kwa nguvu za Roho. Jambo hilo hilo linatokea sasa.

fr.L: Mais de même qu’alors celui qui était né selon la chair persécutait celui [qui était né] selon l’Esprit, ainsi [en est-il] aussi maintenant.
fr.B: À cette époque, le fils né selon la chair persécutait le fils né selon l’Esprit, et il en est de même maintenant.
fr.R: Mais autrefois, le fils né de façon humaine ordinaire maltraitait le fils né par la puissance de l’Esprit. La même chose arrive aujourd’hui.

decisions.choice: persecuted: Paul's reading of Genesis 21:9, where Sarah sees Ishmael with Isaac
alternatives: a stronger word than Genesis supports
decisions.reason: Genesis 21:9 says Sarah saw Hagar's son "laughing" or "playing", a Hebrew word that can also mean mocking; the Greek Old Testament adds that he was playing with Isaac. Genesis does not use a word for persecution. Paul reads the scene as hostility from the older son to the younger, which is how it was often understood among Jews of his time.

decisions.choice: according to the Spirit: born by the power of God's Spirit, who fulfilled the promise
decisions.reason: πνεῦμα here is the Spirit of God. Verse 23 said Isaac was born "through the promise"; now Paul says "according to the Spirit", because it was God's power that gave a child to a barren woman. The Galatians also began with the Spirit (3:2-5).

decisions.choice: born according to the flesh: by ordinary human means, as in verse 23
decisions.reason: σάρξ has the same sense as in verse 23: natural birth by human arrangement. Applied to Paul's day, it describes those who rely on what is done in the body, circumcision (6:12-13).

decisions.choice: so also now: those who insist on the law are pressing hard on those who live by the promise
decisions.reason: Paul means the pressure on the Galatians and on himself from those who demand circumcision (5:11, 6:12). He does not name them here.

decisions.choice: the son born ... the son born
decisions.reason: The Greek has only articles, "the one"; the two sons of verse 22 are meant.

decisions.choice: mistreated
decisions.reason: Genesis tells of a quarrel at home, not of a persecution in the later sense (m1); "mistreated" is plain and fits both scenes. Literal and Balanced keep "persecuted".

en.L: But what does the Scripture say?
en.R: But what do the Scriptures say?

decisions.choice: the Scripture: the particular passage about to be quoted, Genesis 21:10
decisions.reason: γραφή in the singular often means one passage of Scripture. Paul makes it speak, as in 3:8 and 3:22: what it says is what God says.

decisions.choice: the Scriptures
decisions.reason: Readable uses the plural, the ordinary way to speak of the Bible, as in verse 22.

decisions.choice: Andiko (L); Maandiko (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the singular "Andiko", one passage of Scripture (m1). Balanced uses the plural "Maandiko", the ordinary Swahili way of speaking of Scripture, where the English Balanced says "Scripture" without an article.

source.text: Ἔκβαλε τὴν παιδίσκην καὶ τὸν υἱὸν αὐτῆς, οὐ γὰρ μὴ κληρονομήσει ὁ υἱὸς τῆς παιδίσκης μετὰ τοῦ υἱοῦ τῆς ἐλευθέρας.

records.literal_gloss: Cast out the slave woman and the son of her, for no not will inherit the son of the slave woman with the son of the free.

en.L: "Drive out the slave woman and her son, for the son of the slave woman will by no means inherit with the son of the free [woman]."
en.B: "Send away the slave woman and her son, for the slave woman's son will never share the inheritance with the free woman's son."
en.R: "Send the slave woman and her son away. The slave woman's son will never share the inheritance with the free woman's son."

es.L: «Echa fuera a la esclava y a su hijo, porque de ningún modo heredará el hijo de la esclava con el hijo de la libre».
es.B: «Despide a la esclava y a su hijo, porque el hijo de la esclava nunca tendrá parte en la herencia con el hijo de la mujer libre».
es.R: «Manda lejos a la esclava y a su hijo. El hijo de la esclava nunca compartirá la herencia con el hijo de la mujer libre».

sw.L: "Mfukuze mwanamke mtumwa pamoja na mwanawe, kwa maana mwana wa mwanamke mtumwa hatarithi kamwe pamoja na mwana wa [mwanamke] huru."
sw.B: "Waondoe mwanamke mtumwa na mwanawe, kwa maana mwana wa mwanamke mtumwa hatashiriki kamwe urithi pamoja na mwana wa mwanamke huru."
sw.R: "Wapeleke mbali mwanamke mtumwa na mwanawe. Mwana wa mwanamke mtumwa hatashiriki kamwe urithi pamoja na mwana wa mwanamke huru."

fr.L: « Chasse l’esclave et son fils, car le fils de l’esclave n’héritera certainement pas avec le fils de la [femme] libre. »
fr.B: « Renvoie l’esclave et son fils, car le fils de l’esclave n’aura jamais part à l’héritage avec le fils de la femme libre. »
fr.R: « Renvoie l’esclave et son fils. Le fils de l’esclave ne partagera jamais l’héritage avec le fils de la femme libre. »

decisions.choice: a quotation of Genesis 21:10, Sarah's words to Abraham
decisions.reason: In Genesis Sarah says the slave woman's son will not inherit "with my son Isaac". Paul writes "with the son of the free woman" to fit his argument. In Genesis 21:12 God tells Abraham to do what Sarah says, so Paul can quote it as what Scripture says.

decisions.choice: will never inherit: the strongest possible denial
decisions.reason: οὐ μὴ with a future verb rules something out completely.

decisions.choice: inherit: receive what was promised to Abraham's heirs
decisions.reason: κληρονομέω takes up Paul's theme of the inheritance, which comes by promise and not by law (3:18, 3:29, 4:1-7). Only the children of the free woman are heirs.

decisions.choice: drive out: Scripture rules that the way of the law and the way of promise cannot share the inheritance
alternatives: a direct command to expel the teachers
a statement of God's verdict, not a command to the church
decisions.reason: Paul may be telling the Galatians to send away the teachers who demand circumcision, or he may be stating God's verdict that those who rely on the law have no share with the children of promise. Either way the slave woman and her son stand for life under the law (4:24-25).

decisions.choice: Drive out (L); Send away (B, R)
decisions.reason: ἐκβάλλω is a strong word, used of driving out or expelling. Literal keeps that force; Balanced and Readable use "send away", which is what Abraham did in Genesis 21:14.

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave woman" at every level, as in 4:22: the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free.

source.text: διό, ἀδελφοί, οὐκ ἐσμὲν παιδίσκης τέκνα ἀλλὰ τῆς ἐλευθέρας.

records.literal_gloss: Therefore, brothers, not we are of slave woman children but of the free.

en.L: Therefore, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we are not children of a slave woman but of the free [woman].
en.B: So then, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we are children not of a slave woman but of the free woman.
en.R: So, {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}, we are not the children of a slave woman. We are the children of the free woman.

es.L: Por tanto, hermanos, no somos hijos de una esclava, sino de la libre.
es.B: Así que, hermanos, no somos hijos de una esclava, sino de la mujer libre.
es.R: Así que, hermanos, no somos hijos de una esclava. Somos hijos de la mujer libre.

sw.L: Kwa hiyo, ndugu, sisi si watoto wa mwanamke mtumwa, bali wa yule [mwanamke] huru.
sw.B: Basi, ndugu, sisi si watoto wa mwanamke mtumwa, bali ni watoto wa yule mwanamke huru.
sw.R: Kwa hiyo, ndugu, sisi si watoto wa mwanamke mtumwa. Sisi ni watoto wa yule mwanamke huru.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, nous ne sommes pas enfants d’une esclave, mais de la [femme] libre.
fr.B: Ainsi donc, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, nous ne sommes pas les enfants d’une esclave, mais de la femme libre.
fr.R: Alors, {{gender:frères et sœurs|frères}}, nous ne sommes pas les enfants d’une esclave. Nous sommes les enfants de la femme libre.

decisions.choice: a slave woman ... the free woman: the article marks the one free woman
decisions.reason: παιδίσκης has no article, "a slave woman", while τῆς ἐλευθέρας has one, "the free woman". Paul may mean that there is only one free mother, the Jerusalem above (4:26), while slavery can come in more than one form. The difference may also be only a matter of style.

decisions.choice: Therefore: the conclusion of 4:21-30, which also leads into 5:1
decisions.reason: διό draws the conclusion of the allegory. The first sentence of chapter 5 then says what follows from being free; some readers take 4:31 and 5:1 as one thought.

decisions.choice: {{gender:brothers and sisters|brothers}}
decisions.reason: Paul is writing to the whole church in Galatia, women and men, and has just said that in Christ there is neither male nor female (3:28). "Brothers" stays available as the traditional form.

decisions.choice: yule mwanamke huru
decisions.reason: Swahili has no article. The Greek sets "a slave woman" without the article against "the free woman" with it (m1); "yule" (that one) marks the one free woman, and the slave woman is left without it.

decisions.choice: slave woman
decisions.reason: "Slave woman" at every level, as in 4:22: the style guide keeps it where slave is set against free.
